  "reasoning": "All supplied worked answers agree with the mathematics except q-72575. q-72854: adding four times row 1 to row 2 gives (0,3,9). q-72860: subtracting three times row 1 from row 3 makes its third entry 3-3(1)=0. q-130285: subtracting twice row 1 from row 3 makes its second entry 4-2(2)=0. The complements are obtained by removing the specified set from its universal set: q-86587 gives {a,c}; q-102246 gives {n}; q-81203 gives the odd integers 1 through 9; q-105179 gives {2,6,10,14,18}; q-81205 gives the even integers that are not multiples of four; q-105188 gives letters k through z. q-73145: the leading entries sum to 1-3=-2. q-73148: they sum to -7+5+3=1. q-72491: A has leading columns 1,3,4,3 and C has 1,2,2,3, so both fail echelon form; B satisfies it. q-129213: A and B satisfy echelon form, while C has a zero row above nonzero rows. q-72575: under the standard definition, echelon form applies to the entire augmented matrix. A has leading columns 1,2,4,4 and B has 3,2,1, so both fail; C has 1,2,5 and satisfies it. MA explicitly applies a coefficient-matrix-only convention and consequently states B only. Its answer is preserved separately, but its definition and classification of A conflict with standard augmented-matrix echelon form. q-129232: A and C repeat leading columns, and B has a zero row above nonzero rows; all three fail. q-42008: zeroing a21 and a43 produces leading columns 1,2,3,4. Each MA evidence span below comes from that question's own captured worked solution.",
